assumptions: critical_swimming_speed_m_s = 0.4 (~11.4 SL/s), typical adult zebrafish Ucrit.
current_speed_m_s = 0.15 (~4.3 SL/s), well below Ucrit so the animal can hold station.
has_swimbladder = true (zebrafish are physoclistous with a swimbladder).
powered = false and flight_mode = 'none': no flight, stated explicitly; this puts the aerobic-demand laws C14/E3 out of scope.
bladder_volume_surface_ml = 0.04, about 5% of ~0.8 mL body volume.
bladder_volume_at_depth_ml = 0.0389, by Boyle's law at 0.3 m (P0 = 101325 Pa, rho = 1000 kg/m3, g = 9.81 m/s2, ratio 0.9718).
Energy budget (intake 100 J/day, assimilation 0.8, routine 56, activity 24 J/day, mass_change 0) is my own estimate, balanced so assimilated energy equals costs.
genotype_edits = 0 (no edits); the unit and format lean_check expects are unknown.
notes: I couldn't run lean_check, so none of this is verified. I know of no law that blocks the brief. The riskiest additions are the energy-budget keys, mass_change and genotype_edits, because I don't know their expected units or format. If one of them comes back violated or malformed, drop it. Flight and aerodynamic keys are left out on purpose; those laws will return cannot-evaluate or out-of-scope for a non-flying fish.
